unit.can_do_en: accept an invitation and thank the host.

judge.reason: Only register differences (tervetuloo/tervetuloa, tuu/tule); same welcome and invitation.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Thanks! Happy birthday to the birthday boy!

judge.reason: Kiitti/kiitos, onnee/onnea, synttäri/syntymäpäivä are register variants; same meaning.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.gloss_en: Thanks! And thanks for the chocolate balls.

judge.reason: Kiitti/kiitos and suklaapalloist/suklaapalloista are register variants; same thanks for chocolates.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Ole hyvä. Täs on myös pieni lahja.
lines.text_kirja: Ole hyvä. Tässä on myös pieni lahja.
lines.gloss_en: You're welcome. Here's a small present too.

judge.reason: Täs/tässä is a register difference; same content.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text_puhe: Ei ois tarvinnu! Saanks mä avata sen nyt?
lines.text_kirja: Ei olisi tarvinnut! Saanko minä avata sen nyt?
lines.gloss_en: You shouldn't have! Can I open it now?

judge.reason: Spoken contractions (ois tarvinnu, saanks mä) match written forms; same meaning.
Kielest/kielestä is only a dropped ending; same meaning.
Spoken passive opiskellaan is used for 'we study'; written opiskelemme is the same meaning.

forms.why_en: Speech changes the last a to o: tervetuloa becomes tervetuloo. Books write tervetuloa.
After ei (not), the verb loses its ending: tulee becomes tule. Speech says tuu.
A fixed word for 'in, inside', used with tule, 'come'.
Thank you, said by the customer; in casual speech it becomes kiitti.

The partitive in wishes: onnea matkaan, good luck. Speech turns -ea into -ee.
Adds -lle for 'to': syntymäpäiväsankari becomes syntymäpäiväsankarille. Speech shortens the start to synttäri-.
And: joins the coffee and the bun in the order.
Thanking takes -sta, with -i- for more than one: suklaapalloista. Speech drops the last vowel.
The imperative for one person is olla without its ending: ole. 'Ole hyvä' means 'here you are' or 'you're welcome'.
Means 'good!' or 'great!', showing you are happy.
Here: in the inessive, literally 'in this'; said when handing something over. Spoken as täs.

The conditional adds -isi for 'would': olla becomes olisi. Speech shortens olisi to ois.
